### Observed differences

- A13 takes part in more cases: it appears in about 26 in 100 traces in the earlier window and about 35 in 100 in the later window (mean occurrences per trace about 0.9 → 1.2). In both windows A13 occurs only inside traces that also contain A05, A14 and A15, and within those traces its presence rose from about 51 of 79 to about 69 of 86. [OCC011, POS013, REL060, REL112]
- Every activity pair involving A13 moved the same way: co-occurrence with A01 rose from about 26% to 35% of traces while "A01 without A13" fell from about 43% to 31%; with A02 co-occurrence rose from about 15% to 25% while "A02 without A13" fell from about 36% to 22%; with A03 (present in all traces) co-occurrence rose from about 26% to 35%. [REL012, REL026, REL038, REL070]
- The A05/A14/A15 group (its three members always occur together) participates slightly more often, about 40 → 43 in 100 traces, and repeats more: A05 and A15 average about 1.9 → 2.3 occurrences per trace with recurrence support rising from 0.30 to 0.38; A14 averages about 0.96 → 1.13. [OCC004, OCC012, OCC013, POS005, POS014, POS015, REL115]
- Spacing between occurrences of these activities changed in event order: for A01→A05, A05→A14 and A15→A14, pairs at event-distance 1–2 became relatively fewer and pairs at distance 4–5 more frequent. [LAG004, LAG029, LAG085]
- Weaker counter-movements: A02 participates in about 51% → 46% of traces; the A01/A06 pair (always together) in about 69% → 65%, with A01's outgoing share to A06 falling from about 52% to 46% while shares to A05 and A15 rose; the A04/A08/A11/A12 group (always together) rose from about 63% to 67%; A02→A03 pairs occur at longer event distances (distance 3: about 81% → 61%), based on only about 40 observed pairs. [REL016, OCC001, OCC005, DIR001, OCC007, REL044, LAG011]

### Inference

Support level: Weak hypothesis

The evidence suggests that in the later window the behaviour involving A13 together with A05, A14 and A15 is executed in a larger share of cases and with more repetition: A13 appears in about 35 in 100 traces versus about 26 in 100 earlier (only ever alongside the A05/A14/A15 group, whose share rose from about 40 to 43 in 100), and A05/A15 average about 2.3 occurrences per trace versus about 1.9, with repeated occurrences becoming more common (recurrence support 0.30 → 0.38). Supporting signs are the direct participation and occurrence increases, the uniform co-occurrence gains in every pair involving A13 or the group, and the shift of A05/A15 occurrence spacing toward longer event distances. What is missing: the most direct indicators show differences of a size that random re-splits of unchanged data produce roughly a quarter to a third of the time (empirical strengths about 0.6–0.75), the many agreeing relational items all rest on the same underlying trace counts and are not independent confirmations, and no screening baseline is provided to judge how many qualifying items an unchanged process would produce. An important competing explanation is therefore sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows: one skewed assignment of the traces containing these activities to the later window would generate the entire correlated pattern. [OCC011, OCC004, OCC013, REL012, REL026, LAG085]

Other differences: A02 participates in fewer traces (about 51% → 46%) and A02→A03 pairs occur at longer event distances; the A01/A06 pair participates slightly less (about 69% → 65%) with A01's outgoing mix shifting from A06 toward A05/A15; the A04/A08/A11/A12 group participates slightly more (about 63% → 67%). These movements are individually weak and are not folded into the main hypothesis. [REL016, LAG011, OCC001, DIR001, OCC007, REL044]
